evidence.claim: Hilbert's 14th problem asks whether rings of the form K ∩ k[x_1..x_n] are finitely generated. Zariski proved it for small n in 1954, and Nagata found a counterexample in 1959 using a ring of invariants of a linear group action.
The first counterexamples to Hilbert's 14th problem were Nagata's (1958). Later ones in low dimension were built with locally nilpotent derivations.
A survey of counterexamples to Hilbert's 14th problem gives the history and references.
